Volume 23, Part 7

According to the Law, it is improper for the Duke of Zhou to take interest heavier than in Wang Mang's time. Master Guan weighed its weight and said: If the ruler takes <note>as tax or interest</note> seven parts while the people keep only three, then the people will fall ill from labor and become captives of the superior.

# Raising Profit <note>original: 舉嬴</note>

**Records of the Grand Historian: Hereditary House of Han**
Qu Yi said: Truly, people have times of advantage and disadvantage. Marquis Zhao once had an advantage, yet he did not build the High Gate. Last year Qin captured Yiyang, and this year there is a drought. Marquis Zhao does not use this time to relieve the distress of the people, but instead increases his extravagance. This is called "time is depleted, yet he **raises profit**." <note>Note: 'Ying' <gloss>profit/surplus</gloss> was used interchangeably with 'Ying' <gloss>fullness</gloss> in ancient characters.</note>

# Obtaining Profit <note>original: 得贏</note>

**Records of the Grand Historian: Biographies of Turtle and Divining Stalks**
If merchants are not strong, they do not **obtain their profit**.
**Jia Yi: Memorial on Minting Coins**
The nature of minting coins is such that if one does not use cleverness in mixing materials, one cannot **obtain profit**. If the mixing is subtle, the profit is very thick.

# Excess Profit <note>original: 餘贏</note>

**Book of Han: Treatise on Food and Money**
People who pursue profit accumulate **excess profit** to delay the flow of goods in the market, causing prices to soar painfully. <note>Note: 'Painfully' means 'extremely'. It means using surplus wealth to accumulate groups of goods and keep them stagnant for oneself, thus the market price becomes very expensive.</note>
Also, **Zhuangzi**: For a person with a skin disease, the only special thing for them is the soup they eat. <note>unclear: text may refer to hoarding or specific consumption</note>
Where goods are many, there is **excess of them**.

# Collecting Profit <note>original: 收贏</note>

**Book of Tang: Treatise on Food and Money**
What wealth produces must depend on human labor. There are fields, gardens, and granaries where values are light, but the masses consider them wealth. There are circulating and breeding goods where the number is small, but daily one **collects their profit**.
Also, in the eighteenth year of the Kaiyuan era, official fields were again given to capital officials. The prefectures and counties recorded one year's tax money as capital, selecting high-status households to manage it. Monthly they **collected the profit** to supply to provincial officials. Furthermore, the capital for public offices throughout the empire was re-established, **collecting a profit** of sixty percent.
**Jade Dew from the Forest of Cranes**
During the Xuanhe era, bandits disturbed the Zhejiang region. The Imperial Army suppressed them. A proposal was made that for selling wine, selling dregs, and for various transaction fees and shop taxes, the amounts should be slightly increased. These were called "Regulated Funds." When Weng Yanguo became the General Controller, he imitated this method and further **collected profit** from it; these were called "Controlled Funds."

# Registering Profit <note>original: 簿贏</note>

**Book of Tang: Biography of Wang Fangyi**
He was promoted to Governor of Su Prefecture. While locusts plagued Hexi, they alone did not reach Fangyi's territory. The people of other commanderies all traveled with heavily calloused feet to come under Fangyi's governance.

When Cui Cong served as the Deputy Grand Ambassador for the Huainan Circuit overseeing regional affairs, Yangzhou had <unclear>20 characters</unclear> and constructed hundreds of buildings to house people, saving many lives. **The Book of Tang: Biography of Su Ting**
Su Ting served as the Military Governor of the various prefectures of Jiannan. At that time, the Shu region was impoverished and the people were displaced. An imperial decree was issued to collect resources from the mountains, marshes, salt, and iron to sustain them. Su Ting recruited garrison soldiers to pay their employment wages; he opened wells, set up furnaces, and calculated income against expenditures. He used the <term>lei</term> <gloss>surplus</gloss> to purchase grain and expand the current food stores. Cui Cong later abolished all these previous burdensome taxes.

# Spring Surplus <note>original: 春羸</note>

**Huainanzi**
In the first month of Spring, it begins to <term>lei</term> <gloss>expand/emerge</gloss>; in the first month of Autumn, it begins to shrink. In the middle of Spring, it begins to go out; in the middle of Winter, it begins to go in.

# Corner Entanglement <note>original: 觚羸</note>

**Huainanzi**
In ancient times, clothing had no uneven corners, and caps had no <term>gu lei</term> <gloss>cornered entanglement</gloss> patterns.
<margin>Note: The pattern of <term>gu lei</term> refers to something like a horse’s eye cage or linked shields. Having "none" means the cap's design was simply smooth and straight.</margin>

# Void and Surplus <note>original: 虛羸</note>

**Classic of the Way and Virtue <note>The Daodejing, likely referencing a specific commentary or apocryphal version</note>**
<term>Xu lei</term> <gloss>Void and surplus</gloss> lean upon each other, alternating without end.
<margin>Note: When Yin reaches its limit, Yang is born; they alternate and replace each other infinitely.</margin>

# Diminishing Surplus <note>original: 損羸</note>

The moon wanes in its fullness; this is the <term>sun lei</term> <gloss>diminishing of the surplus</gloss>.

# Theft of Surplus <note>original: 盜羸</note>

**Classic of the Way and Virtue**
If the treasury is not full, thieves will not <term>lei</term> <gloss>gain a surplus</gloss>. If the treasury is full, then <term>dao lei</term> <gloss>the theft of the surplus</gloss> leads back to self-injury.

# Assisting the Surplus <note>original: 贊羸</note>

**Classic of the Way and Virtue**
<term>Zan lei</term> <gloss>Assist the surplus</gloss> and enter the outward signs.
<margin>Note: <term>Lei</term> means full. This refers to the position of the Nine Assists; when the assistance is full, one enters the Three Manifestations to see good or bad fortune.</margin>

No, if they're married, then they are made free,
If they no longer live in adultery.
So 'tis not that Marriage can proclaim;
Because that Marriage bears the sacred name;
(But nothing sacred, Satan, is in thee)
So by thy own Bonds bound thou now shalt be.)
For that's the way I made the Bonds at first;
And that's the way I said the Heirs must burst.
So now a Husband wilt thou dare assume?
Then now I'll make thee tremble at thy doom.
And bring thy sacred altar; tell ME where
That as a Priest that ever join'd thy hand:
I tell thee MARRIAGE was design'd for man.
But make the Crosses,* see how all do stand,
In every page where Satan threaten'd there,
For on his head his threatenings all shall fall.
The fourteenth page the Crosses do appear;
And the like on all who ever my word he'll hear.
So now those pieces I do tear the fool,
He now shall know he brought it on himself.
So, if his Back be Brass, he can appear,
For from Iron to Iron my word he'll bear.
He now shall find and feel my iron rod,
If he is come my Subjects to compel,
And boldly triumph of his host in hell.
Then now his hellish host, they may appear
And meet their awful JUDGE now in the air,
And see if they can be match for heaven.
For now the Challenge is by Satan given;
And the mad fool shall know my Power's there;
And now his matchless power, let it be known
When I the Earth a strong foundation laid,
I plac'd for man a double flaming sword;
And now I'll use it perfect like my word:
For every way I've sav'd the TREE of LIFE;
And now I'll use the sword to end the strife.
The Breath of LIFE in Man I sure did breathe;
And Man shall find I will not him deceive.
But as the Devil saith that I'm unjust;
Then like his faith I bid him now to trust;
If they no mercy ever found in ME,
Then now they never shall, they all shall see.

<margin>* The Reader will see the reason of the Crosses in a subsequent page.</margin>

<column-break/>

<sig>D</sig>
So now their power let it to appear;
And meet their awful JUDGE now in the air,
Whose just displeasure they have now provok'd;
And now I bid them fear the coming stroke:
The limits of their space were given by ME:
And that their boasting I shall soon destroy,
And then their wisdom let them all enjoy.
I'll now go on, till I the whole do clear.
And to the eighteenth page I now shall come:
There stands the Cross, and so it shall fall on them;
For as he said the fish did jump in thee,
I tell him now, it so shall fall on one.
So now the fool I'd have him to take care,
If he is hardened now he'th all to fear;
For to my word he'll find that I will stand.
I want not armies now for to command,
But want to see if he's a King supreme,
And by his power can all my subjects gain;
The twentieth page, like him, I'll answer here:
Unto men's peril let them join him here;
For all his Votes must meet him in the air;
For there, I tell you all, will be the sight;
And you, my Friends, below will see the fight;
And then with pleasure you may stand and gaze,
And say we're lost in wonder and amaze.
To see our God stand out a Man of War,
And all his heavenly armies to appear!
For as the Shadow unto thee was seen,
I tell thee plain the Substance will begin;
Shot after shot, I tell thee, fast will fly,
And fiery serpents be seen in the sky:
And for a Type my Thunder it doth stand;*
Flashes of lightning are seen in all your land,†
And so the lightning will to all appear,
And rolling thunder bursting in the air:
With great confusion fast it will be hurl'd,
Wave after wave, and world confus'd with world.
For as the Vision it did first appear,
I tell thee plain, the End will be seen clear;
For all the swords will be seen in the sky,
And fast the shot on every side will fly,
So Satan thou hast challeng'd for a War,
Mark, how the twenty-second page appears;
For in thy own words I shall answer here:

<margin>* See Dispute with the Powers of Darkness, page 96.
† See Strange Effects of Faith, page 29.</margin>
